title: Kessler Shield Vehicle Service Contracts Waiting Period, Authorization and Claim Filing Terms
content:
The same claim-timing terms apply at every Kessler Shield Vehicle Service Contracts coverage level: Kessler Shield Powertrain, Powertrain Plus, Select, Preferred, Exclusionary and Exclusionary Wrap.

| Term | Every coverage level |
|---|---|
| Waiting period: calendar days after the sale date | 30 |
| Waiting period: miles beyond the odometer at sale | 1000 |
| No waiting period on a contract sold on the vehicle's purchase deal | yes |
| Repair must be authorized by claim number before work begins | yes |
| Calendar days after the repair order closes to complete the claim paperwork | 30 |
| Months of maintenance history (manufacturer-scheduled oil and fluid services) to be shown on a claim for a lubricated component | 12 |

**What each figure measures.**
- The day figure counts calendar days from the sale date.
- The mile figure counts miles driven beyond the odometer reading recorded at sale.
- The filing figure counts calendar days from the day the repair order closes.
- The maintenance-history figure counts months back from the failure. It applies only where a claim is for an internally lubricated component (engine, transmission or drive axle).

Because no coverage level departs from these figures, a contract's level never changes its waiting period, its authorization requirement, its filing window or its maintenance look-back.
